To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ah receptor from liver cytosol of rats exists in two forms, an unoccupied form and a TCDD-occupied form, that the two forms have different overall surface charges, that the TCDD-occupied receptor has two forms, one that is similar to the unoccupied receptor and another form with different overall surface charge, and that the TCDD-induced transformation of the Ah receptor is reversible.
the Ah receptor exists in at least two forms in vitro and in liver nuclei of rats treated with TCDD.
the Ah receptor from liver can exist in at least three distinct forms, and these forms are distinguished by their elution profiles on DEAE-Sephaose and their affinities for the DNA-Sepharose column.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor and its ligand, 2,3, 7,8-tetra chlorodibenzo-pdioxin (TCDO).
the biochemical characterization of the Ah receptor.
the biochemical and molecular characterization of the cytosolic receptor for the planar polychlorinated aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the unoccupied Ah receptor is a 110,000 dalton protein with a pI of 5.0 and a sedimentation coefficient of 5S and that the receptor is transformed to a 110, 000 dalton protein (pI 3.5, sedimentation coefficient 4S) in vitro by incubation with TCDD at elevated temperatures and in vivo after treatment of rats with TCDD.

the Ah receptor is a protein complex of at least two components that can exist in at least two distinct forms, the unoccupied and the TCDD-bound form, that are interconvertible in vitro and in the living animal.
the Ah receptor is not a single protein but rather a family of proteins that are interconverted by ligand binding and temperature changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ah receptor is a protein that is found primarily in hepatic cytosol, but can be extracted from the nuclei of TCDD-treated rats and that the unoccupied form can be converted into two occupied forms in vitro and in the nuclei of TC DD-treated rats.
the unoccupied Ah receptor has the ability to transform into a more positively charged form in the presence of TCDF.
the Ah receptor is a ligand-dependent, heat-activated transcription factor that is involved in the control of the expression of a variety of genes in the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ah receptor is a dynamic protein and can exist in multiple forms.
the receptor can be in a number of different conformations, depending on the ligand and conditions, and that these conformations have very different biological activities.
the Ah receptor is a dynamic entity, and that it can undergo a transformation process in vitro and in the intact cell.
